title: Validating AI-Driven Nudge Recommendations: A/B Testing Two-Tower and Bandit Models in Simulated Digital Banking Environment
authors: Kristiana, I.; Prabowo, H.; Gaol, F. L.; Qomariyah, N. N.
venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Computer Society
tldr: An AI model combining a Two-Tower Network for static personalization and a Multi-Armed Bandit for adaptive nudging increases recommendation-following from 13.6% to 52.87% in a simulated mobile banking A/B test.
problem_and_motivation: Existing recommender systems in banking rely on collaborative or content-based filtering, which suffer from sparsity, cold-start problems, and a lack of behavioral awareness. There is a gap in empirically validated models that integrate static personalization with real-time adaptive learning and explicit behavioral nudge design.
approach: A hybrid AI recommendation model was developed using a Two-Tower Network (TWN) for static personalization and a Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) for adaptive nudge selection.
The model was evaluated using a sequential quasi-experimental A/B test with 214 control and 174 treatment participants, all verified bank customers.
The control group (App v1) received rule-based nudges, while the treatment group (App v2) received personalized and adaptive nudges from the TWN+MAB system.
A TWN-only ablation baseline was introduced to isolate the effect of the behavioral nudging and adaptive bandit layer.
The model was trained on data from the control group and deployed to the treatment group, with a Supabase backend logging all user interactions.
Nine nudge mechanisms (e.g., personalization, framing, social proof) were operationalized as the action space for the MAB.
The MAB used an ε-greedy policy and a Gaussian reward formulation for simulation, with real interaction outcomes (purchases) used for final evaluation.
The evaluation focused on total purchase conversion, recommendation-driven conversion, and alignment with the MAB's optimal arm.
A chi-square test (χ² = 6.49, p < 0.0108) was used to assess the statistical significance of differences in recommendation-aligned behavior.
Regret and reward trajectories were analyzed to assess the internal learning dynamics of the MAB.
findings: num: The treatment group showed a higher purchase rate (62.07%) compared to the control group (48.6%).
num: Recommendation-following behavior increased from 13.6% in the control group to 52.87% in the treatment group.
num: 100% of recommendation-driven purchases in the treatment group aligned with the MAB's optimal arm.
num: The treatment effect corresponds to an odds ratio of approximately 7.15 for following recommendations.
num: A chi-square test confirmed the significance of the behavioral shift (χ² = 6.49, p < 0.0108).
The bandit's smoothed regret trajectory remained below thresholds of 0.10 and 0.15, indicating stable learning.
The time-averaged reward curve for the MAB remained stable around a common mean over iterations.
The hybrid model demonstrated consistent outperformance of the rule-based baseline across all major behavioral metrics.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a hybrid AI recommendation model that integrates static personalization (TWN) with adaptive nudge optimization (MAB), validated in a controlled experimental setting. It provides empirical evidence that combining these components significantly influences user financial behavior, specifically increasing recommendation-following rates. The paper addresses a gap in the literature by testing such a model with verified bank customers in a realistic digital simulation. It also establishes a reproducible methodology for evaluating behavioral interventions in digital banking through A/B testing and internal learning diagnostics.
directly_justifies: The hybrid model combining TWN personalization and MAB adaptivity produced nudges that were better matched in context and effectiveness.
The treatment group showed a statistically significant increase in recommendation-following behavior (χ² = 6.49, p < 0.0108).
All 92 recommendation-driven purchases in the treatment group converged on the optimal arm identified by the MAB algorithm.
The smoothed regret trajectory stayed well under a threshold of 0.10 and 0.15, demonstrating stable bandit learning.
limits: The study uses a simulated mobile banking environment, lacking the ecological validity of real financial applications with actual monetary stakes.
The personalization model was trained on a medium-sized, domain-specific corpus, limiting generalizability to users with sparse behavior or underrepresented demographic profiles.
The A/B test was sequential, not parallel, so time-based effects cannot be completely ruled out, making it a quasi-experiment.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan across all topic domains was performed. The paper was flagged as highly relevant to domains 5.A (Financial Behavioral Profiles), 6.A (Predictive Modeling), 11.A (Engagement Dynamics), 12.A (Evaluation Frameworks), and 12.B (Evaluation of Algorithmic Modules) because its core contribution is an AI model that learns from behavioral profiles to predict and influence user engagement, with a strong focus on evaluation. Medium relevance was assigned to 5.C (Classification Approaches) for its use of profiles, 7.E (Cold-Start) for addressing this issue, 9.A and 9.B (Mobile-First/UX) for the simulation environment, 11.B (Retention) for aiming to improve engagement, and 14.B (ML Serving) for describing the deployment. Low or contextual relevance was assigned to 1.C (as the study is on Indonesian, not Filipino, young professionals), 6.B (no explicit forecasting of spending), 7.B (focus on product, not budget, recommendations), and 14.A/14.C (not directly covered). The mapping rationale captures the study's focus on behavioral modeling and system validation, rather than on specific budget allocation, Filipino demographics, or deployment infrastructure.

limitations: Low ecological validity due to the simulated banking environment without real monetary losses.
Limited generalizability due to training on a medium-sized, domain-specific corpus.
Sequential A/B design introduces potential time-based confounds, making it a quasi-experiment [unacknowledged].
Ethical risks regarding personal autonomy and fairness from personalized nudging are acknowledged but not fully addressed.
The model's effectiveness and fairness in production environments with real financial risk were not evaluated.
remember_this: Combining a Two-Tower Network with a Multi-Armed Bandit improved recommendation-following from 13.6% to 52.87%.
The treatment group achieved a 62.07% purchase rate, higher than the 48.6% baseline in the control group.
The statistical significance of the behavioral shift was confirmed (χ² = 6.49, p < 0.0108).
All recommendation-driven purchases in the treatment group aligned with the MAB's optimal arm.
The hybrid model demonstrates a reproducible approach for integrating machine learning with behavioral economics.
